must_remember: Planck's quantum hypothesis states that oscillators emit or absorb energy in discrete packets: $E = h\nu$.
The ultraviolet catastrophe in classical physics predicted infinite energy density at short wavelengths.
Planck's law reduces to the Rayleigh-Jeans law at very long wavelengths ($h\nu \ll k_B T$).
Planck's law reduces to Wien's radiation law at very short wavelengths ($h\nu \gg k_B T$).
Wien's displacement law states that $\lambda_{max} T = b$, where $b = 2.898 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}\cdot\text{K}$.
Stefan-Boltzmann law gives total emissive power as $E = \sigma T^4$.
The average energy of a Planck oscillator is given by $\langle E \rangle = \frac{h\nu}{\exp(\frac{h\nu}{k_B T}) - 1}$.
